sources.title: Historical Volatility of Apple Stock (AAPL) - Macroption
sources.content:
April 2010 - For the first time after the 2007-2009 financial crisis Apple historical volatility fell below 15%. This period also showed probably the greatest short-term change in historical volatility on Apple. Historical volatility over the 21 trading days ending 14 April 2010 was 12.77% (the low) and historical volatility over the 21 days ending on 10 May 2010 was 46.71% (see more details about the volatility spike and the May 2010 Flash Crash above).

## Historical Volatility of Apple in 2008 [...] May 2010 - Of course big part of this volatility spike can be attributed to the Flash Crash of 6 May. However, the 21-day historical volatility of Apple had more than doubled already before the Flash Crash: it was 32.65% on 5 May, compared to 12.77% on 14 April. It further increased in the days following the crash (as the low volatility April days dropped out of the trailing window) and reached high of 48.05% on 19 May. Apple stock price was around 250 in those days; its range on the Flash Crash day itself was 199-258. Also note that the Flash Crash was a textbook example of events that can't be fully reflected in historical volatility, as its calculation typically only uses closing prices. The closing price on the Flash Crash day was 246.25, down "only" 10 dollars from the previous day's [...] Historical volatility of Apple was ranging between 15% and 30% for most of the time in 2009-2012, with occasional spikes to 40% or slightly above and a few dips below 15%. Below you can see charts of 21-day and 63-day historical volatility of Apple from 2006 to January 2013:

21-day historical volatility of AAPL 63-day historical volatility of AAPL

## Notable Spikes in Apple Stock Historical Volatility

End of 2012 - Realized volatility of Apple started to increase after the stock reached its all time high in September 2012. At that time the volatility was well below 20% and it gradually grew to above 40% in November and December.

result.synthesized_summary:
Here is a concise financial-research summary of the provided source:

According to "Historical Volatility of Apple Stock (AAPL) - Macroption" (https://www.macroption.com/historical-volatility-of-apple-stock-aapl), Apple's historical volatility fell below 15% for the first time after the 2007-2009 financial crisis in April 2010. However, it spiked to 46.71% by May 10, 2010, partly due to the May 2010 Flash Crash. The 21-day historical volatility more than doubled from 12.77% on April 14, 2010, to 32.65% on May 5, 2010, and reached 48.05% on May 19, 2010. From 2009-2012, Apple's historical volatility ranged between 15% and 30%, with occasional spikes to 40% or above. By the end of 2012, realized volatility increased after the stock reached its all-time high in September 2012, growing from below 20% to above 40% in November and December.
